name: Remote Work Visitor Visa ("Digital Nomad Visa")

requirements.blocker_text: Requires verifiable proof of employment with, or freelance work conducted entirely for, a company or clients based outside South Africa -- authorised specifically under Section 11(1)(b)(iv) of the Immigration Act 13 of 2002 as a variant of the Visitor's Visa, not as a standalone visa category, formally distinguishing it from South Africa's other work_sponsored visas.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the employing or contracting entity is genuinely based outside South Africa.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires gross annual income of at least ZAR 650,976, evidenced by 3 months of bank statements -- reduced from an initially proposed ZAR 1,000,000 threshold via the Third Amendment to the Immigration Regulations, published 9 October 2024. Applicants aged 18+ only.
requirements.fix_path: Document gross annual income at or above the current threshold via 3 months' bank statements.

evidence_required.document: 3 months' bank statements evidencing the qualifying income
Proof of employment/contracting with a foreign-based entity
International health insurance covering the full stay, police clearance from countries of 12+ months' residence in the past 5 years

outcome.duration_length: up to 12 months initially, renewable annually up to a total of 3 years
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: working more than 6 months within any rolling 36-month period triggers a South African Revenue Service (SARS) registration requirement, per DHA/Fragomen guidance

sources.title: WTS Renmere -- The South African Digital Nomad Visa, confirming the Section 11(1)(b)(iv) legal basis and the formal designation 'Remote Work Visitor Visa'
RSM South Africa -- Go Digital, Go Global: South Africa launches nomad visa, describing the October 2024 Third Amendment and the reduced ZAR 650,976 income threshold

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a dha.gov.za page was achieved for this route in this research pass, despite very extensive, near-unanimous cross-corroboration of the core facts across 8+ independent sources. MINOR LIVE DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than silently resolved: most sources cite the income threshold as ZAR 650,976/year, but one source (ibn.co.za) states ZAR 650,796 -- a very close but genuinely different figure, most likely a transposition typo in one source rather than two distinct real figures, but not conclusively resolved against a primary source in this research pass; ZAR 650,976 is used here as the majority-corroborated figure. STRUCTURAL FINDING, a genuinely troubled and lengthy legislative history worth stating plainly: this visa was first introduced in framework form on 28 March 2024, went through an incomplete public-comment process, was implemented in a first version effective 20 May 2024, then revised again ('Take 3' per multiple law-firm sources) via the Third Amendment to the Immigration Regulations on 9 October 2024 -- which is also when the income threshold was cut by roughly a third, from the originally proposed ZAR 1,000,000 down to the current ZAR 650,976 -- and the visa reportedly only became fully operational for applications in March 2025, nearly a year after the framework legislation was first introduced. Legally, this is NOT a standalone visa category but a variant of the ordinary Visitor's Visa (Section 11(1)(b)(iv)) -- a structural classification choice worth surfacing, since it means this route's legal DNA is closer to za_visitor_visa than to South Africa's other work-authorisation categories, despite functioning in practice as a dedicated digital-nomad product; classified work_independent here based on function rather than its formal Visitor's Visa lineage. leads_to_pr and leads_to_citizenship are correctly false: no source identified any pathway from this visa toward permanent residence or citizenship, consistent with the pattern seen on Thailand's DTV and Poland's/Brazil's digital-nomad routes documented elsewhere in this dataset.
